method: MIXED, AND DELIBERATELY ASSEMBLED FROM FIVE SEPARATE AMH PAGES. AMH's Probiotics topic is four sentences long; the rest of what AMH says about probiotics is scattered across its Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, diarrhoea and eczema topics, and this guideline gathers all five so the pattern is visible. All AMH content is paraphrased, no passage stored. S1 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP evidence-based review of probiotics for infantile colic (August 2022 -- FOUR YEARS OLD, stated in the guideline), quoted verbatim including its strain names and its one dose. S2 is one paragraph of an OPEN RACGP AJGP article on paediatric functional abdominal pain disorders (June 2025), quoted verbatim, used ONLY for its Cochrane finding on probiotics. This guideline makes NO general recommendation about probiotics, because none of its sources does.

claims.claim: Infantile colic is a benign, self-limiting condition affecting approximately 20% of all infants worldwide, with symptoms peaking around the sixth week of age and ceasing naturally after 4 to 6 months
claims.source_text: Infantile colic is a benign, self-limiting condition and is a common problem during early childhood, affecting approximately 20% of all infants worldwide. … Symptoms peak around the sixth week of age, with symptoms ceasing naturally after 4-6 months of age.

claims.claim: The Rome IV diagnosis of infantile colic requires ALL of: the infant under five months of age when symptoms start and stop; recurrent or prolonged crying, agitation and irritability reported by caregivers occurring without obvious cause and not preventable or resolvable by them; and ABSENCE of infantile failure to thrive, fever or illness
claims.source_text: According to Rome IV criteria, the diagnosis of infantile colic requires all of the following: infant under five months of age when the symptoms start and stop; periods of recurrent and/or prolonged crying, agitation and irritability reported by caregivers, which occur without any obvious cause and cannot be prevented or resolved by caregivers; and absence of infantile failure to thrive, fever or illness.
